responses.title: The Purpose of This Course
responses.html:
This course is designed to help you become a professional data scientist by building tangible, real-world skills.

  • Read broadly to develop intuition.
  • Complete open-ended work without being told every step.
  • Apply concepts rather than merely memorize definitions.

responses.title: Readings
responses.html:
Expect reports, blog posts, and textbook chapters—often on topics beyond the day’s lecture.

Plan on roughly one hour of reading per week.

You are expected to remember the central ideas, and readings may appear on exams.

responses.title: Academic Integrity
responses.html:
All suspected cheating is referred to OSC.

  • Do not use prohibited help or materials during exams.
  • Do not submit code you cannot understand or explain.
  • You should be able to reproduce familiar Python patterns and summarize your own reports.
  • Everything you submit should be reproducible by you.

triggers: what if my work is late
responses.title: Late Work
responses.html:
Work submitted after the deadline receives a zero.

If you have a reason you need additional time, explain the situation during office hours. Extensions will generally be granted when requested directly.

responses.title: Class Policies
responses.html:
• Lectures are not recorded; a weekly topic recap will be posted.
  • Laptops and phones require an ADS accommodation; tablets are permitted.
  • If illness prevents your best effort on an exam, stay home and arrange an alternative.
  • Do not come to office hours while ill.

responses.title: Class Code of Conduct
responses.html:
• Criticism of the instructor and teaching is allowed.
  • Harassment, inflammatory posts, and criticism directed at TAs or classmates are not.
  • Meme posts are welcome when they remain appropriate.
  • Do not make other students feel unwelcome.

triggers: what does a data scientist do
responses.title: What Is a Data Scientist?
responses.html:
A data scientist combines three roles:

Programmer
Machine-learning expert
Statistician

They usually advise other parts of a company by turning raw data into useful decisions—and, ultimately, economic value.

triggers: what are some data science applications
responses.title: Examples of Data Science
responses.html:
Drug efficacy
Use trial results to determine whether a treatment works.
Movie recommendation
Predict what someone will enjoy from past ratings.
Image recognition
Identify what appears in a labeled image.
Credit risk
Predict whether a borrower will repay a loan.

responses.title: Getting Data
responses.html:
Data may be:

  • Gathered from external sources
  • Retrieved from existing company databases
  • Collected by tools you create
or

Design an experiment that produces the data you need.

responses.title: Data Processing
responses.html:
Most real-world data will be bad.

Before analysis, you will need to address:

  • Duplicates
  • Inconsistent formatting
  • Strange outliers
  • Incorrect values and other mistakes

triggers: what do we look for in data
responses.title: Data Exploration
responses.html:
When you receive a large body of raw data, begin by asking:

  • What is actually here?
  • Are there interesting relationships or correlations?
  • Is anything important missing?
  • Do we have what we need to answer the question?

responses.title: Modeling
responses.html:
A model is a module that uses data to predict the future.
  • The model is often the primary deliverable.
  • Its predictions may determine company policy or live operational decisions.

responses.title: Convincing People You’re Right
responses.html:
A correct analysis has little value if decision-makers do not understand or trust it.

Translate technical evidence into a clear explanation of what the model does, why it is credible, and what action should follow.
